trigger: a settings row whose version column is '' / uppercase / non-hex (out-of-band SQL, including the repair the manual prescribes)
summary: parse_row copies version from the DB without is_version_text, so a bad version reads as a valid document: GET returns 200 with a version the client cannot send back, replace is 400 (parse_put/put accept only 64 lowercase hex), create(none) is 409 carrying the same unusable version; only SQL repairs it; it is not Corrupt although the store header says stored rows are never silently defaulted. Derived from I5 case c (wedges a state machine). Orchestrator confirmed parse_row line 134 has no version check.
classification_rationale: header read-rule says stored rows are validated; version is not

trigger: an ITServiceOwner revoked/demoted or the group re-parented while a PUT waits on the 3 s lease and 10 s lock_timeout after the authority read and the synchronous requested audit row
summary: authority is read once, then up to about 13 s can pass before COMMIT with no re-check. Mechanical derivation is I1/E5 = HIGH. Orchestrator assessment (NOT an adjudication, the orchestrator may not adjudicate its own rejection): the write serialises before the revoke, every precedent site has the same check-then-act shape, and the group-owner path is dormant (sec-F1), which argues I9. Needs a non-author adjudicator to de-escalate or an in-transaction recheck.
classification_rationale: revocation is not honoured for an in-flight request

trigger: 20,001 or more settings rows (a global writer creating groups, documents, and deleting groups leaves orphans that count)
summary: list_all refuses past kListRowCap (TooMany) but put() enforces no matching bound and no DELETE route or reaper exists, so the write side can reach a state the read side rejects: list route and every host route answer 503 until SQL. Architect AR-2 sharpened it: the host route needs only the device's chain yet calls list_all(); the read rule IS the write validator.
